questions.stem: If two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated with distance '$d$' and placed in a medium of dielectric constant $K$. What will be the equivalent distance between charges in air for the same electrostatic force?
questions.solution:
$F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{kd^2}$ (in medium), $F_{air} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{d'^2}$

$F = F_{air} \Rightarrow kd^2 = d'^2 \Rightarrow d' = d\sqrt{k}$

questions.stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x = -A$ and $x = +A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x = 0$ to $\dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2$ s; then time taken by particle in going from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
questions.solution:
Using the reference circle: from $0$ to $A/2$, $\omega t_1 = \pi/6$; from $A/2$ to $A$, $\omega t_2 = \pi/3$.

$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow t_2 = 2t_1 = 2\times 2 = 4$ s

questions.stem: A wire of resistance $160\,\Omega$ is melted and drawn in wire of one-fourth of its length. The new resistance of the wire will be
questions.solution:
Volume constant: $A_1L = A_2\dfrac{L}{4} \Rightarrow A_2 = 4A_1$

$\dfrac{R_2}{R_1} = \dfrac{L_2A_1}{A_2L_1} = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{16} \Rightarrow R_2 = \dfrac{160}{16} = 10\,\Omega$

questions.stem: The dimensional formula of latent heat is -

questions.stem: Electric potential at a point '$P$' due to a point charge of $5 \times 10^{-9}$ C is $50$ V. The distance of '$P$' from the point charge is: (Assume, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$)
questions.solution:
$V_P = \dfrac{KQ}{r} \Rightarrow 50 = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times5\times10^{-9}}{r}$

$r = \dfrac{45}{50} = 0.9$ m $= 90$ cm

questions.stem:
A gas can be taken from A to B via two different processes ACB and ADB.

When path ACB is used $60$ J of heat flows into the system and $30$ J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used work done by the system is $10$ J. The heat flow into the system in path ADB is:
questions.solution:
$\Delta Q_{ACB} = \Delta W_{ACB} + \Delta U_{ACB} \Rightarrow 60 = 30 + \Delta U \Rightarrow \Delta U = 30$ J

$\Delta U_{ADB} = \Delta U_{ACB} = 30$ J (state function)

$\Delta Q_{ADB} = \Delta U_{ADB} + \Delta W_{ADB} = 30 + 10 = 40$ J
questions.subtopic: First law; path independence of internal energy

questions.stem: A long straight wire of radius $a$ carries a steady current $I$. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\dfrac{a}{2}$ and $2a$ from the axis of the wire is:
questions.solution:
Inside ($r = a/2$): $B_1\cdot 2\pi\dfrac{a}{2} = \mu_0\dfrac{I}{4} \Rightarrow B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$

Outside ($r = 2a$): $B_2\cdot 2\pi(2a) = \mu_0 I \Rightarrow B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$

So $B_1 = B_2 \Rightarrow 1:1$
questions.subtopic: Ampere's law: field inside and outside a wire

questions.stem: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position '$x$' as a function of time '$t$' is given as $x = (t^3 - 6t^2 + 20t + 15)$ m. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is:

There are two long co-axial solenoids of same length $l$. The inner and outer coils have radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ and number of turns per unit length $n_1$ and $n_2$, respectively. The ratio of mutual inductance to the self-inductance of the inner-coil is:
Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with speed of $1.5 \times 10^8\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. The relative permeability of the medium is $2.0$. The relative permittivity will be:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{\varepsilon_m\mu_m}{\varepsilon_0\mu_0} = \dfrac{1/v^2}{1/c^2} \Rightarrow \varepsilon_r\mu_r = \dfrac{c^2}{v^2}$

$\varepsilon_r \times 2 = \dfrac{(3\times10^8)^2}{(1.5\times10^8)^2} = 4 \Rightarrow \varepsilon_r = 2$
questions.subtopic: Speed of EM waves in a medium

questions.stem: The range of the projectile projected at an angle of $15^\circ$ with horizontal is $50$ m. If the projectile is projected with same velocity at an angle of $45^\circ$ with horizontal, then its range will be :
questions.solution:
$R = \dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$. At $15^\circ$: $50 = \dfrac{u^2\sin 30^\circ}{g} \Rightarrow \dfrac{u^2}{g} = 100$ m.

At $45^\circ$: $R = \dfrac{u^2}{g} = 100$ m

questions.stem: In an ac circuit, an inductor, a capacitor and a resistor are connected in series with $X_L = R = X_C$. Impedance of this circuit is :
questions.solution: $Z = \sqrt{(X_L - X_C)^2 + R^2} = R \quad (\because X_L = X_C)$

questions.solution:
Given lights are of same wavelength, hence stopping potential will remain same.

questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.stem: A light string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ (where $m_2 > m_1$). If the acceleration of the system is $\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$, then the ratio of the masses $\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}$ is :
questions.solution:
$a = \left(\dfrac{M_2 - M_1}{M_1 + M_2}\right)g \Rightarrow \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} = \left(\dfrac{M_2 - M_1}{M_1 + M_2}\right)g$

$M_1 + M_2 = \sqrt{2}M_2 - \sqrt{2}M_1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}$

questions.stem: The ratio of the shortest wavelength of Balmer series to the shortest wavelength of Lyman series for hydrogen atom is :
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda_L} = RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2}\right)$, $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_B} = RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2^2}\right)$

$\dfrac{\lambda_B}{\lambda_L} = 4:1$

questions.stem: A block of mass $1$ kg is pushed up a surface inclined to the horizontal at an angle of $60^\circ$ by a force of $10$ N parallel to the inclined surface as shown in the figure. When the block is pushed up by $10$ m along the inclined surface, what is the work done against frictional force? $g = 10\,\text{m/s}^2$.
questions.solution:
Friction $f = \mu mg\cos 60^\circ = 0.1 \times 1 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$ N

$W = f \cdot d = 0.5 \times 10 = 5$ J

questions.solution:

questions.stem: The temperature of an ideal gas is increased from $200$ K to $800$ K. If r.m.s. speed of gas at $200$ K is $v_0$. Then, r.m.s. speed of the gas at $800$ K will be:

questions.stem: Pressure inside two soap bubbles are $1.01$ and $1.02$ atmosphere, respectively. The ratio of their volumes is:
questions.solution:
$\Delta P_1 = P_1 - P_0 = 0.01 = \dfrac{4T}{R_1}$ and $\Delta P_2 = P_2 - P_0 = 0.02 = \dfrac{4T}{R_2}$

Angular spread $= 2\theta = 60^\circ$

questions.stem: A solid metallic cube having total surface area $24\,\text{m}^2$ is uniformly heated. If its temperature is increased by $10^\circ$C, calculate the increase in volume of the cube. (Given $\alpha = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\,^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$)

$6a^2 = 24 \Rightarrow a = 2$ m, $V = 8\,\text{m}^3$. $\gamma = 3\alpha = 1.5\times10^{-3}\,^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$

$\Delta V = V\gamma\Delta T = 8 \times 1.5\times10^{-3}\times 10 = 0.12\,\text{m}^3 = 1.2\times10^5\,\text{cm}^3$

questions.stem: Two bodies of mass $1$ kg and $3$ kg have position vectors $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $-3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ respectively. The magnitude of position vector of centre of mass of this system will be similar to the magnitude of vector:
questions.solution:
$\vec{r}_{com} = \dfrac{m_1\vec{r}_1 + m_2\vec{r}_2}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{1(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}) + 3(-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{1+3} = -2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$

$|\vec{r}_{com}| = \sqrt{4+1+1} = \sqrt{6}$

Check: $\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}: \sqrt{6}$; $-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}: \sqrt{14}$; $-2\hat{i}+2\hat{k}: \sqrt{8}$; $-2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}: 3$

Correct answer is (A).

questions.stem:
Among the following the correct statements are:

I. $\text{LiH}$, $\text{BeH}_2$ and $\text{MgH}_2$ are saline hydrides with significant covalent character

II. Saline hydrides are volatile

III. Electron-precise hydrides are Lewis bases

IV. The formula for chromium hydride is CrH

The correct option is:
questions.solution:
I is correct: $\text{LiH}$, $\text{BeH}_2$, $\text{MgH}_2$ have significant covalent character. II is wrong: saline hydrides are non-volatile crystalline solids. III is wrong: electron-precise hydrides (e.g. $\text{CH}_4$) are neither Lewis acids nor bases; electron-rich hydrides are Lewis bases. IV is correct: chromium forms the metallic hydride CrH.

Hence I and IV only.

questions.stem:
In which of the following reactions does $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ act as an oxidising agent (either in acidic, alkaline or neutral medium)?

(i) $2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$

(ii) $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 6\text{H}^+ + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$

(iii) $\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow$

(iv) $\text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow$
questions.solution:
Completing the reactions:

(i) $\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(ii) $\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(iii) $\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{I}^- + \text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

(iv) $\text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{4+} + \text{OH}^-$

In reactions (i) and (iv), $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as oxidising agent and itself gets reduced.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a water soluble vitamin, that is not excreted easily?
questions.solution:
Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in liver and adipose tissue; water-soluble vitamins (B-complex and C) are usually not stored and excess is excreted in urine.

However, Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ (cobalamin) is an exception: the body can store it in the liver for several years, so it is not excreted as easily as $\text{B}_1$, $\text{B}_2$ or $\text{B}_6$.

The correct answer is Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism present in nitropentammine chromium (III) chloride is
questions.solution:
The formula is $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$. It can exist as $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$ (pentaamminenitrochromium(III) chloride) and $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{ONO})]\text{Cl}_2$ (pentaamminenitritochromium(III) chloride).

Therefore the isomerism is linkage isomerism, as the $\text{NO}_2$ group is linked through N as $-\text{NO}_2$ or through O as $-\text{ONO}$.

questions.stem: Identify, from the following, the diamagnetic, tetrahedral complex
questions.solution:
(a) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$; $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing: $sp^3$, tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

(b) In $[\text{Co}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$, oxalate is bidentate, giving an octahedral structure.

(c) In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand causing pairing of 3d electrons: $dsp^2$, square planar and diamagnetic.

(d) In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, Ni is in zero oxidation state ($3d^84s^2$). CO is a strong field ligand causing pairing of 3d and 4s electrons: $sp^3$, tetrahedral and diamagnetic.

Hence (D) is the correct answer.

The Prime Minister's recent trip to Nigeria, the first bilateral prime ministerial visit to Africa since Jawaharlal Nehru's 45 years ago, recalls a long neglected Indian obligation. "It is up to Asia to help Africa to the best of her ability," Nehru told the Bandung Conference in 1955, "because we are sister continents." The Prime Minister's proposed strategic partnership with African nations might at last make good that 52-year old promise and also, perhaps, challenge China's expedient diplomacy.

In the intervening years, the West's sanctimonious boycott of many African regimes - after nearly a century of extreme colonial exploitation - left the continent in the grip of oppressive rulers looking for new political sponsors, arms-sellers and trading partners. Not only was it an abdication of the developed world's responsibility to the world's least developed region, sanctions actually compounded the sufferings of poorer Africans. The Darfur killings continue and there is no mellowing of Robert Mugabe's repression in Zimbabwe.

Abandoned by the West, Africa looked elsewhere. Beijing filled the vacuum by eagerly embracing dangerous and unsavoury regimes in its search for oil and other minerals. China demonstrated its influence by playing host to 48 out of 53 African leaders a year ago in a jamboree that was historic as well as historical. Historic because China has succeeded in becoming the pre-eminent outside power in Africa and its second biggest trading partner. Historical because modern Chinese diplomacy draws on the Middle kingdom's ancient formula; the tribute system. It was how the son of Heaven brought those nations whom the Celestial Empire called "barbarians" into his imperial trading and, through it, cultural and political system.

Contemporary China's economic penetration of Africa also heralds a new era of cultural and political ties though the Chinese foreign ministry repeatedly assure the world that "our cooperation is not designed to be against or preclude any third party." This is untrue in a world of finite resources. Once the Chinese are established in a country no one else gets a foothold. Myanmar, where India failed to obtain the desired gas concessions, is a prime example. Aware that the hunt for energy is a zero-sum game, China's leadership courts African leaders with regular visits and substantial grants.

After decades of neglect - Vajpayee's Africa visit over a decade ago was to attend a Commonwealth Summit - India will have to move cautiously but quickly if it is to break China's monopoly. Along with investing in Africa's human capital, China has outlined a strategic investment plan to build three to five trade economic cooperation zones in Africa by 2009 to boost trade, which is expected to tap \$40 billion this year. That could double to \$30 billion by 2010 on the back of an insatiable demand for natural resources to feed China's booming economy.

against India entering into a competition with China

questions.solution:
Near $0$: $\log\cos x \approx -\dfrac{x^2}{2}$, $\log(1 + x) \approx x$, so $f(x) \approx -\dfrac{x^3}{2} \to 0 = f(0)$: continuous.

$f'(0) = \lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{f(x)}{x} = \lim\limits_{x\to0}\left(-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right) = 0$: differentiable.

questions.stem: The function $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$ is
questions.solution:
**For injective:** $f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow \dfrac{x_1}{\sqrt{1 + x_1^2}} = \dfrac{x_2}{\sqrt{1 + x_2^2}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{x_1^2}{1 + x_1^2} = \dfrac{x_2^2}{1 + x_2^2} \Rightarrow x_1^2 = x_2^2$; since $x_1, x_2$ have the same sign, $x_1 = x_2$. So $f$ is injective.

**For surjective:** $y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}} \Rightarrow x^2(1 - y^2) = y^2 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{\dfrac{y^2}{1 - y^2}}$, requiring $\dfrac{y^2}{1 - y^2} \geq 0 \Rightarrow y \in (-1, 1)$.

So $f$ is not surjective.

questions.stem: If $x$ is a complex root of the equation $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x \\ x & 1 & x \\ x & x & 1 \end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix} 1 - x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 - x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 - x \end{vmatrix} = 0$, then $x^{2007} + x^{-2007} =$

questions.stem: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of same order such that $AB + BA = X$ and $AB - BA = Y$, then $(XY)^T =$
questions.solution:
$(XY)^T = Y^TX^T$. Since $A, B$ are symmetric, $X^T = (AB + BA)^T = B^TA^T + A^TB^T = BA + AB = X$ and $Y^T = (AB - BA)^T = BA - AB = -Y$.

$\therefore (XY)^T = Y^TX^T = (-Y)X = -YX$

(Equivalently, expanding: $(XY)^T = (BA)(BA) + (BA)(AB) - (AB)(BA) - (AB)(AB) = (BA - AB)(BA + AB) = -YX$.)

questions.stem: If the straight lines $2x + 3y - 1 = 0$, $x + 2y - 1 = 0$, and $ax + by - 1 = 0$ form a triangle with the origin as the orthocentre, then $(a, b)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Point A is the intersection of AB ($2x + 3y = 1$) and AC ($x + 2y = 1$). A line through A: $(x + 2y - 1) + \lambda(2x + 3y - 1) = 0$ ...(i)

It passes through the orthocentre $(0, 0)$: $-1 - \lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$, giving $x + y = 0$ as AD.

Since $AD \perp BC$: $-1 \times \left(-\dfrac{a}{b}\right) = -1 \Rightarrow a + b = 0$

Similarly, BE $\perp$ CA gives $a + 2b = 8$.

Solving: $a = -8$, $b = 8$

questions.stem: The coefficient of the highest power of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(x + \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\right)^8 + \left(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\right)^8$
If $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + 1\cdot2}\right] + \tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + 2\cdot3}\right] + \ldots + \tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + n(n + 1)}\right] = \tan^{-1}[x]$, then $x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2 - 1}{1 + 1\cdot2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3 - 2}{1 + 2\cdot3}\right) + \ldots + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{(n + 1) - n}{1 + n(n + 1)}\right) = \tan^{-1}x$

$\Rightarrow [\tan^{-1}2 - \tan^{-1}1] + [\tan^{-1}3 - \tan^{-1}2] + \ldots + [\tan^{-1}(n + 1) - \tan^{-1}n] = \tan^{-1}x$

$\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}(n + 1) - \tan^{-1}1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{1 + (n + 1)}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{n + 2}\right) \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{n}{n + 2}$

questions.stem: If $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ are complex numbers such that $|z_1| = |z_2| = \ldots = |z_n| = 1$, then $|z_1 + z_2 + \ldots + z_n|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$|z_k| = 1 \Rightarrow z_k\bar{z}_k = 1 \Rightarrow \bar{z}_k = \dfrac{1}{z_k}$

$|z_1 + z_2 + \ldots + z_n| = |\bar{z}_1 + \bar{z}_2 + \ldots + \bar{z}_n| = \left|\dfrac{1}{z_1} + \dfrac{1}{z_2} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{z_n}\right|$

questions.stem: If $z, \bar{z}, -z, -\bar{z}$ form a rectangle of area $2\sqrt{3}$ square units, then one such $z$ is
questions.solution:
Let $z = x + iy$, so $\bar{z} = x - iy$. The vertices of the rectangle are $(x, y), (x, -y), (-x, -y), (-x, y)$.

Area $= (2x)(2y) = 4xy = 2\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow 2xy = \sqrt{3}$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $y = \sqrt{3}$ satisfies this, so $z = \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{3}i$

questions.stem: $f(x) = \dfrac{\cos x}{\left[\dfrac{2x}{\pi}\right] + \dfrac{1}{2}}$, where x is not an integral multiple of $\pi$ and $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is
questions.solution:
$f(-x) = \dfrac{\cos(-x)}{\left[-\dfrac{2x}{\pi}\right] + \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{\cos x}{-1 - \left[\dfrac{2x}{\pi}\right] + \dfrac{1}{2}}$ (as $x$ is not an integral multiple of $\pi$)

$= -\dfrac{\cos x}{\left[\dfrac{2x}{\pi}\right] + \dfrac{1}{2}} = -f(x)$

Therefore, $f(x)$ is an odd function.

questions.stem: The maximum volume (in cu. units) of the cylinder which can be inscribed in a sphere of radius 12 units is
questions.solution:
$12^2 = r^2 + \left(\dfrac{h}{2}\right)^2$, $V = \pi r^2h = \pi\left(144 - \dfrac{h^2}{4}\right)h = 144\pi h - \dfrac{\pi}{4}h^3$

$\dfrac{dV}{dh} = 144\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{4}h^2 = 0 \Rightarrow h^2 = 48 \times 4 \Rightarrow h = 8\sqrt{3}$

$12^2 = r^2 + 48 \Rightarrow r^2 = 96$

Volume $= \pi r^2h = \pi \times 96 \times 8\sqrt{3} = 768\sqrt{3}\pi$

questions.stem: $\displaystyle\int_5^9 \dfrac{\log 3x^2}{\log 3x^2 + \log(588 - 84x + 3x^2)}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$588 - 84x + 3x^2 = 3(14 - x)^2$, so $I = \displaystyle\int_5^9 \dfrac{\log 3x^2}{\log 3x^2 + \log 3(14 - x)^2}dx$ ...(i)

Using $\displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a + b - x)dx$:

$I = \displaystyle\int_5^9 \dfrac{\log 3(14 - x)^2}{\log 3(14 - x)^2 + \log 3x^2}dx$ ...(ii)

Adding: $2I = \displaystyle\int_5^9 dx = 9 - 5 = 4 \Rightarrow I = 2$

questions.stem: The area of the region bounded by the curves $x = y^2 - 2$ and $x = y$ is
questions.solution:
Solving $x = y^2 - 2$ and $x = y$: $(-1, -1)$ and $(2, 2)$.

$A = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} y\,dy - \int_{-1}^{2}(y^2 - 2)\,dy = \left[\dfrac{y^2}{2} - \dfrac{y^3}{3} + 2y\right]_{-1}^{2}$

$= \left(2 - \dfrac{8}{3} + 4\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} - 2\right) = \dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{27}{6} = \dfrac{9}{2}$

questions.stem: Let ABC be a triangle and $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ be the position vectors of A, B, C respectively. Let D divide BC in the ratio $3:1$ internally and E divide AD in the ratio $4:1$ internally. Let BE meet AC in F. If E divides BF in the ratio $3:2$ internally then the position vector of $F$ is
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{OD} = \dfrac{1\cdot\vec{b} + 3\vec{c}}{1 + 3} = \dfrac{\vec{b} + 3\vec{c}}{4}$

$\overrightarrow{OE} = \dfrac{4\overrightarrow{OD} + \overrightarrow{OA}}{4 + 1} = \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 3\vec{c}}{5}$

Also $\overrightarrow{OE} = \dfrac{2\overrightarrow{OB} + 3\overrightarrow{OF}}{2 + 3} \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{OF} = \dfrac{5\overrightarrow{OE} - 2\overrightarrow{OB}}{3} = \dfrac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 3\vec{c} - 2\vec{b}}{3} = \dfrac{\vec{a} - \vec{b} + 3\vec{c}}{3}$

questions.stem: The angle between the lines whose direction cosines are given by the equations $3l + m + 5n = 0$, $6mn - 2nl + 5lm = 0$ is
questions.solution:
From $3l + m + 5n = 0$: $m = -3l - 5n$. Substituting in $6mn - 2nl + 5lm = 0$:

$6(-3l - 5n)n - 2nl + 5l(-3l - 5n) = 0 \Rightarrow (n + l)(2n + l) = 0 \Rightarrow l = -n$ or $l = -2n$.

If $l = -n$: $m = -2n$. If $l = -2n$: $m = n$.

Direction ratios: $1, 2, -1$ and $-2, 1, 1$; direction cosines $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}}, \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{6}}$ and $\dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{6}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$.

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{-2 + 2 - 1}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{6} \Rightarrow \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)$

questions.stem: The probability that a certain electronic component fails when first used is $0.10$. If it does not fail immediately, the probability that it lasts for one year is $0.99$. The probability that a new component will last for one year is
questions.solution:
$P(F) = 0.10$, $P(F') = 0.90$. Let $E$ be the event that a new component lasts for one year.

$P(E) = P(F)P(E|F) + P(F')P(E|F') = 0.10 \times 0 + 0.90 \times 0.99 = 0.891$

questions.stem: If the focus of parabola $(y - k)^2 = 4(x - h)$ always lies between the lines $x + y = 1$ and $x + y = 3$ then
questions.solution:
Focus is $(h + 1, k)$. It should lie on the opposite side of the origin with respect to $x + y - 1 = 0$ and on the same side as the origin with respect to $x + y - 3 = 0$.

$h + 1 + k - 1 > 0$ and $h + 1 + k - 3 < 0 \Rightarrow 0 < h + k < 2$

questions.stem: The sum of the infinite series $1 + \dfrac{5}{6} + \dfrac{12}{6^2} + \dfrac{22}{6^3} + \dfrac{35}{6^4} + \dfrac{51}{6^5} + \dfrac{70}{6^6} + \ldots$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$S = 1 + \dfrac{5}{6} + \dfrac{12}{6^2} + \dfrac{22}{6^3} + \ldots$, $\dfrac{S}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{5}{6^2} + \dfrac{12}{6^3} + \ldots$

Subtracting: $\dfrac{5}{6}S = 1 + \dfrac{4}{6} + \dfrac{7}{6^2} + \dfrac{10}{6^3} + \ldots$

$\dfrac{5}{36}S = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{4}{6^2} + \dfrac{7}{6^3} + \ldots$

Subtracting: $\dfrac{25}{36}S = 1 + \dfrac{3}{6} + \dfrac{3}{6^2} + \ldots = 1 + \dfrac{3/6}{1 - 1/6} = \dfrac{8}{5}$

$S = \dfrac{288}{125}$

questions.stem: Let the acute angle bisector of the two planes $x - 2y - 2z + 1 = 0$ and $2x - 3y - 6z + 1 = 0$ be the plane P. Then which of the following points lies on P?
questions.solution:
$P_1: x - 2y - 2z + 1 = 0$, $P_2: 2x - 3y - 6z + 1 = 0$

$\dfrac{x - 2y - 2z + 1}{3} = \pm\dfrac{2x - 3y - 6z + 1}{7}$

Since $a_1a_2 + b_1b_2 + c_1c_2 = 20 > 0$, the negative sign gives the acute bisector:

$7x - 14y - 14z + 7 = -[6x - 9y - 18z + 3] \Rightarrow 13x - 23y - 32z + 10 = 0$

$\left(-2, 0, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ satisfies it.

questions.stem: The sum of all values of $x$ in $[0, 2\pi]$, for which $\sin x + \sin 2x + \sin 3x + \sin 4x = 0$, is equal to :
questions.solution:
$(\sin x + \sin 4x) + (\sin 2x + \sin 3x) = 0 \Rightarrow 2\sin\dfrac{5x}{2}\left\{\cos\dfrac{3x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right\} = 0 \Rightarrow 2\sin\dfrac{5x}{2}\left\{2\cos x\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right\} = 0$

$\sin\dfrac{5x}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, \dfrac{2\pi}{5}, \dfrac{4\pi}{5}, \dfrac{6\pi}{5}, \dfrac{8\pi}{5}, 2\pi$

$\cos\dfrac{x}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pi$; $\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

Sum $= 6\pi + \pi + 2\pi = 9\pi$
